✓ Measles.fact: In most places where measles is endemic, the World Health Organization recommends immunization at 9 months of age and again at 18 months of age. ✓ Measles.question: Pneumonia is the most common fatal complication of measles infection and accounts for 56–_____ of measles-related deaths
✓ Measles.fact: == Prognosis == Most people survive measles, though in some cases, complications may occur.  About 1 in 4 individuals will be hospitalized and 1–2 in 1,000 will die.  Complications are more likely in children under age 5, adults over age 20, and pregnant people.  Pneumonia is the most common fatal complication of measles infection and accounts for 56–86% of measles-related deaths.  Possible consequences of measles virus infection include laryngotracheobronchitis, sensorineural hearing loss, and—in about 1 in 10,000 to 1 in 300,000 cases—panencephalitis, which is usually fatal.  Acute measles encephalitis is another serious risk of measles virus infection.  It typically occurs two days to one week after the measles rash breaks out and begins with very high fever, severe headache, convulsions and altered mentation
